tldr: The target is the matched centered \(L_2\) homogeneity-testing radius in the full latent causal class \(\mathcal M\), with an unknown Hölder propensity and baseline regression of exponent one tenth, a Lipschitz effect, and a public wrapped Laplace measurement channel. The open comparison is whether the full class retains the non-novel randomized reference radius \(n^{-2/13}\) or requires a strictly slower nuisance-learning radius, including every necessary logarithmic factor. A twice-inverted close-pair contrast with exact constant-effect profiling supplies the finite-sample upper handle. Normalized same-class homogeneous and separated priors, compared through their actual convolved likelihoods at every record order, supply the converse handle. Only their matched full-class conclusion is the publication-level target. The binary benchmark offers a prospective complement to differential-variance detection with a mismeasured modifier.
gap: The non-novel randomized inverse-testing reference is \(n^{-2/13}\). Direct CATE estimation and circular density testing do not determine whether unknown rough propensity and baseline functions preserve that radius or impose a slower full-class radius. The missing comparison requires a constant causal effect in every null-mixture component after actual observation-channel convolution.
fill: The load-bearing results are finite-sample profiled full-class attainment and a matching all-test converse from normalized observed mixtures. Their joint optimization determines the radius relative to \(n^{-2/13}\), with every logarithmic factor. The randomized marked-Fourier lemma supplies only a supporting sanity reduction.
